issues.failure_explanation: Theorem 3.3 asserts that for any t in [0,T], there exists a deterministic linear subspace V of H = L^2(D) with dimension O(|log(eps)|^2) that approximates u(t) with error O(eps) in L^2(Omega; H). In the proof, the subspaces V_1, V_2 (and V_4, V_5, V_6 in Appendix A.4) are defined via basis elements that depend on the sample path of W(t) and on t. They are sample-path-dependent (random) and time-varying subspaces, not a fixed deterministic subspace V of H. If random subspaces were permitted, any 1-dimensional space span{u(t)} would yield error 0, rendering the claim trivial. For deterministic subspaces V of H, the claim is mathematically false: driving Wiener noise excites all spatial modes, causing the eigenvalues of the covariance operator of u(t) to decay algebraically (polynomially) rather than exponentially; thus by Karhunen-Loeve theory, any deterministic subspace achieving error eps in L^2(Omega; H) requires dimension polynomial in 1/eps, not O(|log(eps)|^2).

failure_location.quote:
Then for each $t$, $w_{\epsilon}$ sits in the linear space 
$$V_1=	ext{span} \Big\{\sum_{k=1}^{M_{\epsilon}}c_k(-1)^l\frac {(\lambda_kt-\mu t)^l}{l!}e^{q_k W(t)}\phi_k(x), l=0,1\cdots,L_{\epsilon}\Big\}.$$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must abandon the O(|log(eps)|^2) dimension bound and reformulate the result with dimension polynomial in 1/eps, constructing a true deterministic subspace from the leading eigenfunctions of the covariance operator of u(t).
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 3.3 is invalidated. The claim that parabolic SPDE solutions admit logarithmic-dimensional data space approximations in L^2(Omega; H) fails; only polynomial dimensions in 1/eps can be guaranteed.
issues.title: Parabolic SPDE solution space dimension proof relies on random and time-dependent subspaces and contradicts algebraic spectrum decay
issues.why_classification: The logarithmic dimension bound is a primary theoretical claim of Section 3.2, and repairing it requires replacing the logarithmic rate with a polynomial dimension bound and completely redesigning the proof architecture via covariance spectral analysis.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
The differentiability of $G(s,t)$, i.e., $G(s,t)\in \mathcal C^{p}([0,T]^2)$ leads to 
$\lambda_j= o(j^{-(p+1)})$ (see, e.g., \cite{MR728689}).

issues.failure_explanation: The proof of Lemma 3.4 deduces that the two-time correlation kernel G(s,t) is C^p([0,T]^2) in time from the spatial C^p differentiability of the stochastic flow x -> X_{s,t}(x). This deduction is false because Brownian motion W(t) is only Holder continuous with exponent < 1/2 in time. Even for smooth velocity c(x) = 1 and smooth initial data u_0(x) = cos(x), the solution is u(t,x) = cos(x - W(t)), yielding G(s,t) = pi * E[cos(W(t) - W(s))] = pi * exp(-|t - s| / 2). This kernel has a sharp corner across s = t and is not even C^1([0,T]^2). Its eigenvalues decay as lambda_j ~ j^{-2} regardless of p, so sum_{j=k+1}^infty lambda_j ~ k^{-1}, contradicting the claimed lambda_j = o(j^{-(p+1)}) and the dimension bound o(eps^{-2/p}).

failure_location.quote: Since $X_{s,t}(\cdot)$ is $\mathcal C^{p}$-differentiable, one can also show that $G(s,t)$ is $\mathcal C^{p}$-differentiable since $c(\cdot)$ and its derivatives up to order $p$ are bounded thanks to the compactness of $\mathcal D$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must acknowledge the non-smoothness of G(s,t) across the diagonal s=t caused by Brownian motion and weaken the dimension bound to O(eps^{-2}) based on the actual O(j^{-2}) spectral decay of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-type covariance operators.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 3.4 is invalidated. The subspace dimension bound o(eps^{-2/p}) fails; the dimension cannot improve arbitrarily with the smoothness order p of u_0 and c.
issues.title: Temporal regularity of covariance kernel for hyperbolic SPDE falsely inferred from spatial flow regularity
issues.why_classification: The claim that higher initial/velocity regularity p yields dimension o(eps^{-2/p}) is fundamentally defeated by the non-differentiability of Brownian paths at s=t, requiring a major weakening of the result.

issues.failure_explanation: In Proposition 3.6, the target is the mean trajectory E[u(t)] = sum_k E[c_k] e^{i lambda_k t} e^{-q_k^2 t / 2} phi_k(x). The approximating vector w_eps is defined using the random initial coefficients c_k. In bounding ||E[u_{M_eps}] - w_eps||_{L^2(Omega; H)}^2, the proof erroneously treats c_k and E[c_k] as equal, dropping the difference (E[c_k] - c_k). For random u_0, the true difference contains sum_k Var(c_k) e^{-q_k^2 t}, which does not vanish as L_eps -> infty. Furthermore, the constructed subspace V_t is defined using the sample-dependent random coefficients c_k and depends on t through the non-factorable terms (q_k^2 t / 2)^l / l!, so it does not yield a fixed deterministic subspace V of dimension O(|log(eps)|^2).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must restrict to deterministic initial data u_0 (so c_k = E[c_k]) and resolve the time-dependence of the basis vectors in V_t to produce a valid fixed subspace V.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition 3.6 is invalidated; the proof fails to establish that E[u(t)] is approximated by a deterministic logarithmic-dimensional subspace when u_0 is random.
issues.title: Invalid truncation error bound and random/time-dependent space in stochastic Schrödinger equation analysis
issues.why_classification: The step in the proof conflates a random variable with its expectation, leaving an irreducible variance term that defeats the error bound whenever the initial condition is random as hypothesized.
